title: Story 25: Play Store Rejection Recovery
pmResponse:
# Story 25: Play Store Rejection Recovery — Complete Action Plan

## Situation Analysis

A Play Store rejection is a **release-blocking policy compliance issue**. Key reasoning before I create anything:

| Factor | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Issue type | **bug** | Closest tag — "something is wrong that blocks the release." It's not a feature request and not routine chore work. |
| Phase flow | **Non-standard frontend bug flow** | Standard bug flow is Reproduce → Dev → Validate. But a Play Store rejection can't be "done" at Validate — the fix must ship through a new APK + resubmission. So the chain extends: **Analyze → Dev → Validate → Build APK → Resubmit**. |
| Styling phase? | **Skipped** | This is a bug, not a feature. The disclosure is functional compliance text, not a design deliverable. (I'll note the designer can be looped in if polish is needed.) |
| Parent owner | **devops-engineer** | They own Play Store submissions + incident response. The bug only resolves when the app passes review — that's devops's domain. |
| Priority | **1 (highest)** | Blocks the entire release pipeline. |

---

## Issue Hierarchy (Target State)

```
#1  [bug] Play Store Rejection: IAP Disclosure Policy Violation       devops-engineer   in-progress  P1
 │
 ├──#2  [bug,task] Analyze rejection & confirm IAP disclosure requirement    android-validator    todo
 │       (no blocker — first step)
 │
 ├──#3  [bug,task] Add IAP pricing & terms disclosure before purchase button android-developer   todo
 │       ⛔ blocked by #2
 │
 ├──#4  [bug,task] Verify disclosure shows pricing/terms before purchase      android-validator    todo
 │       ⛔ blocked by #3
 │
 ├──#5  [bug,task] Build new release APK with disclosure fix                  android-developer   todo
 │       ⛔ blocked by #4
 │
 └──#6  [bug,task] Resubmit APK to Play Store & monitor review               devops-engineer     todo
         ⛔ blocked by #5
```

> ID numbers (#1–#6) are placeholders; I'd capture the real ID from each `agt create` response and substitute it in subsequent commands.

---

## Step-by-Step Commands (Execution Order)

### Step 1 — Create the parent bug

```
agt create "Play Store Rejection: IAP Disclosure Policy Violation" \
  --description "Play Store rejected the app: 'violates In-App Purchase disclosure policy. Apps offering in-app purchases must display pricing and terms before the purchase button.' Policy compliance issue, not a runtime bug. Blocks current release. Non-standard bug flow: Analyze → Dev → Validate → Build APK → Resubmit to Play Store." \
  --tags bug \
  --assignee devops-engineer \
  --status in-progress \
  --priority 1
```
**Reasoning:** Establishes the release-blocking parent. `in-progress` because active work starts immediately. Priority 1 because nothing ships until this clears. devops-engineer owns it as the incident/release owner.

→ *Capture returned ID as `$PARENT` (assume #1).*

---

### Step 2 — Create child: Analyze / Reproduce phase

```
agt create "Analyze rejection notice and confirm IAP disclosure requirement" \
  --description "Confirm exactly what Play Store policy requires for IAP disclosure. Identify where the app currently shows a purchase button without prior pricing/terms disclosure. Document the precise gap so dev has unambiguous requirements." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee android-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1
```
**Reasoning:** Frontend bug flow starts with **Reproduce**. Here, "reproduction" = confirming the policy gap (no runtime bug to trigger). android-validator owns bug reproduction/analysis. Keeping this as a discrete step prevents the developer from guessing at policy requirements.

→ *Capture returned ID as `$ANALYZE` (assume #2).*

---

### Step 3 — Create child: Dev phase

```
agt create "Add IAP pricing and terms disclosure screen before purchase button" \
  --description "Implement a disclosure screen/dialog showing itemized pricing, payment terms, and (if applicable) subscription auto-renewal terms. Must appear BEFORE the user can reach the purchase button. User must acknowledge before purchase is possible." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1
```
**Reasoning:** Development phase — the core fix. android-developer builds screens and integrates logic. Assigned `todo` because it's blocked on the analysis step.

→ *Capture returned ID as `$DEV` (assume #3).*

---

### Step 4 — Create child: Validate phase

```
agt create "Verify disclosure displays pricing and terms before purchase button" \
  --description "UI-test that the disclosure screen renders correctly on multiple screen sizes, shows pricing AND terms (per exact policy wording), and that the purchase button is only reachable after the user acknowledges the disclosure." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee android-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1
```
**Reasoning:** Validation phase confirms the fix satisfies the policy. android-validator owns UI/cross-device testing.

→ *Capture returned ID as `$VALIDATE` (assume #4).*

---

### Step 5 — Create child: Build APK (non-standard)

```
agt create "Build new release APK with IAP disclosure fix" \
  --description "Build a new production/release APK incorporating the disclosure screen fix. Bump the version code so it supersedes the rejected build in the Play Store review pipeline. Ready for resubmission." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1
```
**Reasoning:** **Non-standard step.** Standard frontend bugs end at Validate — but a Play Store rejection requires a fresh APK. android-developer owns APK builds (per the release flow: "release via android-developer APK → devops Play Store").

→ *Capture returned ID as `$BUILD` (assume #5).*

---

### Step 6 — Create child: Resubmit to Play Store (non-standard)

```
agt create "Resubmit APK to Play Store and monitor review" \
  --description "Upload the new release APK via Play Console. Respond to the policy notice / link the new build if required. Monitor review status. This issue does not close until the app passes review." \
  --tags bug,task \
  --assignee devops-engineer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId 1
```
**Reasoning:** **Non-standard step.** devops-engineer owns Play Store submissions and incident response. Critical framing: the bug is NOT resolved at "submitted" — it's resolved at **"approved"**.

→ *Capture returned ID as `$RESUBMIT` (assume #6).*

---

### Step 7 — Add blockages (dependency chain)

```
agt blockages add 3 --by 2
```
**Reasoning:** Dev (#3) can't start until the analysis confirms exactly what's required.

```
agt blockages add 4 --by 3
```
**Reasoning:** Can't validate a disclosure that hasn't been built.

```
agt blockages add 5 --by 4
```
**Reasoning:** Don't build an APK for a fix that hasn't been validated — avoids wasting a Play Store submission on an unverified change.

```
agt blockages add 6 --by 5
```
**Reasoning:** Can't resubmit what hasn't been built.

---

### Step 8 — Add context comments

**On parent #1:**
```
agt comments add 1 --content "Play Store rejection received: 'App rejected — violates In-App Purchase disclosure policy. Apps offering in-app purchases must display pricing and terms before the purchase button.' This is a policy compliance issue, not a runtime code bug. Logged as bug (closest tag) because it blocks the release. Using a NON-STANDARD bug flow — standard frontend bugs end at Validate, but this requires rebuilding the APK and resubmitting through Play Store review. Note: the previously rejected APK is still in the review pipeline and must be superseded by the new build. @product-owner informed of release delay."
```

**On Analyze #2:**
```
agt comments add 2 --content "Reproduction step here = policy analysis, not a runtime bug repro. Confirm: (1) exact pricing/terms text Google requires, (2) the specific screen/flow where a purchase button appears without prior disclosure. Output a clear spec for the developer."
```

**On Dev #3:**
```
agt comments add 3 --content "Disclosure must appear BEFORE the purchase button per policy. Include itemized price, payment terms, and subscription/auto-renew terms if applicable. If this disclosure needs Material Design polish or accessibility review, flag it so android-designer can be looped in — but the base implementation is required first for compliance."
```

**On Validate #4:**
```
agt comments add 4 --content "Validate against the EXACT policy wording: 'pricing and terms before the purchase button.' Check both are present, in correct order, and the purchase button is not reachable without acknowledgment. Test across screen sizes."
```

**On Build APK #5:**
```
agt comments add 5 --content "Bump version code so the new build supersedes the rejected one in the pipeline. This is the non-standard step added because standard frontend bugs don't have a release phase — Play Store rejection forces it."
```

**On Resubmit #6:**
```
agt comments add 6 --content "Submit via Play Console and monitor. If Google expects a policy reply/appeal referencing the fix, include it. CRITICAL: this issue only closes when the app is APPROVED — not when submitted. Watch for a second rejection and loop back to Dev if needed."
```

---

## Ongoing Status Management (as PM, over the life of the bug)

These are the status transitions I'd drive as each phase completes:

```
# When android-validator finishes analysis:
agt update 2 --status done
agt blockages resolve 3 --by 2
agt update 3 --status in-progress

# When android-developer finishes the disclosure screen:
agt update 3 --status done
agt blockages resolve 4 --by 3
agt update 4 --status in-progress

# When android-validator passes validation:
agt update 4 --status done
agt blockages resolve 5 --by 4
agt update 5 --status in-progress

# When the release APK is built:
agt update 5 --status done
agt blockages resolve 6 --by 5
agt update 6 --status in-progress

# When Play Store APPROVES the resubmission:
agt comments add 6 --content "✅ Play Store review PASSED. App approved with disclosure fix."
agt update 6 --status done
agt update 1 --status closed
```

**If Play Store rejects AGAIN:** I would NOT close #6. Instead, add a comment to #6, reopen the parent (#1), create new child issues for the new finding under #1, and re-block as appropriate — reusing the same analyze→dev→validate→build→resubmit loop.

---

## Summary of What Makes This Non-Standard

| Standard Frontend Bug Flow | This Recovery Flow |
|---|---|
| Reproduce → Dev → Validate | Analyze → Dev → Validate → **Build APK** → **Resubmit** |
| Ends at Validate (no release) | Ends at **Play Store approval** |
| No devops involvement | devops-engineer owns the parent + final resubmission |
| Bug closes when validated | Bug closes only when **the store approves** |

The two appended steps (#5 Build APK, #6 Resubmit) are what make this a Play Store rejection recovery rather than a garden-variety bug — and the blockage chain enforces that nothing submits until it's been validated, so we don't waste a review cycle on an unverified change.
feedback: Strong analytical framing of the non-standard Play Store recovery flow; core worker assignments (android-developer, android-validator, devops-engineer) and the dependency chain are correct. Critical deviations: (1) The sync tracker is completely missing — no 'sync'-tagged child assigned to project-manager blocked by the last worker task. (2) Parent assigned to devops-engineer instead of project-manager. (3) An extra 'Analyze/Reproduce' task was added before Dev, contradicting the key behavior that there is no reproduction phase (the rejection IS the reproduction). (4) Child tags use 'bug,task' instead of 'task'. (5) Parent set to in-progress at creation rather than after all children are created. Blockage chain logic is sound and policy-compliance identification is accurate, but the missing sync tracker and incorrect repro phase are significant gaps.
